title: A link leads to page 12, but sheet 12 is needed: a PDF numbering error
description: In the PDF there are three introductory pages, so sheet 12 is on page 15. We examine link parameters, page labels and the internal index without rebuilding the volume.
seo_title: A link leads to page 12, but sheet 12 is needed: a PDF numbering error
seo_description: In the PDF there are three introductory pages, so sheet 12 is on page 15. We examine link parameters, page labels and the internal index without rebuilding the volume.
seo_keywords: PDF page numbering, link to project sheet, PDF page, page labels
content:
A link from the project registry opens a PDF, but instead of the required calculation it shows another page. The file itself is complete, sheets are not rearranged and the revision is correct. The cause may be mixing the ordinal page number in the file with the number printed on the sheet itself. Correcting the link in such a case does not require rebuilding the volume or requesting missing materials.

Where sheet number 12 is located

Consider a conditional volume R-8, hosted over HTTPS. At the beginning there are three unnumbered introductory pages. Then the main part starts with visible number 1 and continues sequentially without gaps. Consequently, the sheet with printed number 12 occupies the fifteenth place from the start of the PDF. The number 12 on the sheet image itself is correct.

The registry entered a link of the form tom-r8.pdf#page=12. In the viewer used, it has been verified: the page parameter addresses the ordinal page of the file, counting the first as 1. Therefore the twelfth physical page opens. Because of the three introductory pages, the number 9 is printed on it. The user sees an unexpected section and reports that the calculation is lost, although the sought sheet is three pages further.

For this specific structure, the correct numeric link ends in #page=15. It leads to physical page 15 with printed number 12. The number changed in the navigation address; the project sheet number and the volume content remained the same. There is no reason to remove the three introductory pages for the numbers to match.

Three values that are easy to confuse

A PDF page may have an ordinal number starting from 1, an internal index starting from 0 and a separate label. For the sought sheet of our volume these are respectively 15, 14 and, if labels are set in accordance with the main part, "12". The printed digit is part of the visible content and by itself does not configure these navigation properties of the file.

The internal index 14 also should not be substituted into the page parameter: in the addressing scheme considered, it expects a number starting from 1. Then #page=14 would lead to the sheet with visible number 11. After eliminating the three-page offset, a second, already one-page error can be obtained if the starting point is confused.

PDF Association separately describes the difference between index, number and page label. Adobe documentation shows creating links with the page parameter and using named destinations. Here the verified behavior of a specific viewer is considered. One cannot promise that any embedded viewer on any site will process all URL parameters in the same way.

Why manual entry of "12" sometimes works correctly

Some programs can navigate by page label. Then the user enters 12 in the navigation field and lands on the needed physical page 15. It does not follow that a URL with page=12 uses the same rules. The interface field and the link parameter handler may interpret the entered number differently. It is important to check the actual transition used by the registry recipient.

Editing labels is also not the same as printing new numbers on sheets. A label can improve navigation while preserving visible content. But it does not turn the fifteenth physical page into the twelfth by order. Therefore after setting labels one cannot automatically consider that old numeric links were corrected: they may continue to address the previous place in the file.

One addition does not work for the whole archive

In our simple volume, the offset of plus three applies uniformly to the whole main part. If a separate appendix with its own numbering appears in the middle or a new document begins with sheet 1, a single formula will no longer be sufficient. Two different sheets may have one visible number. The navigation registry will require the document context and the actual position of each target sheet.

When a new introductory page is added, old sheet 12 will already be in physical place 16. The numeric link page=15 will continue to open the fifteenth page, but that will be a different sheet. That is why link control is needed when updating the volume, even if the target calculation number has not changed. Named destinations may reduce dependence on such a shift, if they are correctly created and supported by the system used.

How to close the remark to the registry

For R-8 it is enough to state: the required sheet 12 is present on physical page 15; the previous link erroneously led to page 12 with visible number 9. After correction, check the transition and read the main inscription of the target sheet. Successful opening of the PDF without such a check does not yet confirm correct addressing.

If there are many such breaks in the electronic set, send a request to institute "Nedra" for checking navigation of the project volume. Attach the source PDF and the link registry. This helps find the page correspondence error without presenting the address correction as a new revision of the technical solution.
